thread:
sre_oncall: :rotating_light: Seeing a sudden spike in 502/503 from the hosted API immediately after today's deploy (12:02 UTC). Error pattern: upstream reset / stream closed. Start ~12:03.
alice_prodeng: I'm checking canary routing and model variants. Can confirm canary group got ~8% traffic and error rate jumped to ~18% for that slice.
bob_infra: Looking at config change — there's a rollout that touched route-weight parsing for the /v1/generate router. Pulling logs now.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: release=canary-2026-03-25T12:02:34 commit=ab12cde canary=8% author=tim_eng
sre_oncall: Tim, can you reproduce from prod edge? Need a quick repro to confirm gateway vs model runtime.
tim_eng: Repro attempt from eu-west1:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-v1","input":"short test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
# {"error": "gateway: stream closed (kv-cache miss)"}
```
alice_prodeng: Gateway logs show repeated `upstream reset` to backends handling kvcache-based routing. Also seeing malformed route metadata in the routing table for the new canary: `weight: 1000` (should be 0-100).
bob_infra: Whoa — weight parser didn't clamp. In the deploy diff there was a small change in `route_weights` YAML -> int coercion. If a config author accidentally left a large number it skewed the traffic calc and overloaded a small pool.
julie_support: Customer tickets coming in: several customers reported elevated 5xx between 12:03-12:09. I'm prepping a status update.
sre_oncall: Action: rollback canary routing to previous stable weights. Bob, can you roll that back? We'll coordinate on-call.
bob_infra: Initiating rollback of routing patch at 12:05 UTC. Command run:
```
kubectl apply -f /configs/routing/weights/stable.yaml --context=prod
# rollout restart deploy/gateway-router
```
bob_infra: Rollback applied at 12:06 UTC. Starting to shift traffic back.
deploy-bot: config-apply succeeded: config_hash=ff34aa
sre_oncall: Monitoring: error rate dropping — 503/502 count down to baseline by 12:08. Latency improving. :white_check_mark:
tim_eng: Quick note on repro: the failing requests were mostly with Authorization header + long prompt prefix; that code path touches prefix/KV cache which amplified the overload on the misweighted pool.
julie_support: Sent interim message to customers acknowledging the incident and rollback at 12:09 UTC. Will follow up with RCA when available.
alice_prodeng: Root cause: YAML->int parser allowed values >100. When route weight became 1000, traffic math assigned disproportionate share to a small canary pool, causing connection saturation and gateway upstream resets.
alice_prodeng: Fix: add validation in the config service to clamp/validate 0<=weight<=100 and add a dry-run check in the deploy pipeline. Also will add a canary traffic sanity gate (max delta from baseline).
tim_eng: I'll open a follow-up PR to add unit tests for weight parsing and add an alert if any single pool's weight > 100.
bob_infra: Ops action items: 1) tighten rollout speed for routing changes; 2) add canary capacity headroom checks; 3) add rollback automation for weight anomalies.
sre_oncall: Postmortem owners: alice_prodeng (root cause & config fixes), bob_infra (deploy pipeline guardrails), tim_eng (tests & alerts), julie_support (customer comms). Target doc by EOD tomorrow.
julie_support: Logged IDs of affected customers and timelines; coordinating proactive outreach now.
alice_prodeng: Will also add a pre-deploy lint that rejects weight values outside allowed range.
sre_oncall: Thanks everyone — incident closed for now. If errors reappear reopen thread. :handshake:
